newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Wednesday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, livestock dealers said.
Prices were pressured by active hog marketings late last week and on Tuesday, which supplied packers with enough hogs to fill their limited demand, they said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $58.00 at plants, sources said. Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $56.00 to $56.50 in the country and up to $57.00 at plants. Trade was light in Illinois, sources there said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants. Indiana hog prices also were pressured by a "good" movement of hogs early, with not a lot of demand, one livestock dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, Ohio sources said.
Cash hog price declines were furthered by weak pork demand, which stifled packer buying by keeping operating margins in the red, they said.
Pork cutout values on Tuesday were quoted down $0.55 to $0.67 per cwt, USDA reported.
